record.paper_title: (E,E′N) and (E,E′NN) Experiments at NIKHEF, Mainz and JLab and Open Problems in One- and Two-Nucleon Emissions
record.original_question: Which kinematic conditions and final-state selections make exclusive two-nucleon knockout reactions most sensitive to nucleon-nucleon correlations rather than to meson-exchange, isobar, and other two-body current mechanisms? This remains open because the triple-coincidence cross section does not factorize in terms of the two-hole spectral density even without final-state interactions, so extracting correlation information requires identifying observables where correlation effects dominate the competing current contributions.

evidence.quote: Even without FSI the two-hole spectral density is not factorized in the triple coincidence cross section. This makes a difficult task to extract information on correlations from data, and models are required to investigate suitable kinematic conditions where the cross section is particularly sensitive to correlations.

In contrast, (e,e′pp) reactions, where two-body currents play a minor role, are better suited to look for correlations, and resolution of discrete final states has been shown to provide an interesting tool to discriminate between contributions of different mechanisms responsible for two-nucleon emission.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider exclusive electron-induced two-nucleon knockout reactions of the form A(e,e'NN) on a nuclear target A, in which an incoming electron scatters to a detected final electron while two outgoing nucleons N (either pp or pn) are detected in triple coincidence with the scattered electron, leaving the residual (A−2) nucleus in a specified discrete final state. The cross section receives contributions from (i) nucleon–nucleon short-range and tensor correlations in the initial-state nuclear wave function, (ii) two-body meson-exchange currents (MEC), (iii) intermediate isobar (e.g., Δ) excitation currents, and (iv) final-state interactions (FSI) between the outgoing nucleons and the residual system. Even in the absence of FSI, the triple-coincidence cross section does not factorize as a product of an elementary electron–nucleon-pair cross section times the two-hole spectral density of the target, so correlation information cannot be read off directly from the measured cross section.

Problem: Determine the kinematic conditions (e.g., choices of momentum transfer q, energy transfer ω, missing momentum, missing energy, relative and center-of-mass momentum of the outgoing pair, super-parallel vs. other kinematics) and final-state selections (channel pp vs. pn, choice of discrete final state of the residual nucleus, angular configurations of the detected nucleons) under which the exclusive A(e,e'NN) cross section is maximally sensitive to ground-state nucleon–nucleon correlations and minimally contaminated by meson-exchange, isobar, and other two-body current mechanisms. Identify observables (cross sections, ratios, or polarization/asymmetry observables) for which the correlation contribution dominates over the competing two-body current contributions.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work indicates partial progress: (e,e'pp) reactions on selected discrete residual states (notably to the 0+ ground state of the (A−2) system) and super-parallel kinematics, with appropriate cuts on missing momentum and xB ≥ 1.2, Q² > 1.8 GeV², have been identified theoretically and experimentally as conditions where short-range/tensor correlations dominate over MEC and Δ-isobar currents, while (e,e'pn) channels are dominated by two-body currents. However, a complete model-independent identification of optimal kinematics and observables remains under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Electroinduced two-nucleon knockout and correlations in nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: (e,e'pp) cross sections are predicted to exhibit sizeable sensitivity to short-range correlations; (e,e'pn) is dominated by two-body currents.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical work has identified the (e,e'pp) channel and resolution of discrete final states as preferred for isolating NN correlations.

status_evidence.title: Exclusive Studies of Short Range Correlations in Nuclei using CLAS12
status_evidence.snippet: Events where knocked-out nucleons belong predominantly to SRC pairs can be selected with xB ≥ 1.2 and Q² > 1.8 GeV² and limited missing mass.
status_evidence.claim: Experimental kinematic cuts that enhance SRC sensitivity have been identified and are being used at JLab.

status_evidence.title: Exclusive studies on short range correlations in nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of exclusive measurements selecting SRC-dominated kinematics.
status_evidence.claim: Active experimental program continues to refine kinematic selections sensitive to NN correlations.
